messages:
Sam: FYI triaging three support tickets asking for better streaming + tool/function semantics. Customers: AcmeHealth, FinCorp, EduOS.

Sam: Key asks in plain words:
- emit structured JSON fragments early so consumers can act on events
- allow function/tool call metadata to surface while stream is active
- robust fallback when model emits malformed JSON mid-stream

Sam: Example from AcmeHealth: "we need to start sending events to our workflow as they arrive; waiting for full completion breaks UX."

Maya: @Sam can you paste the ticket links and priority? need to slot into roadmap / launch criteria review. :eyes:

Sam: Links and priorities:
- https://support.redwood/acme/12345 (P1, product demo next month)
- https://support.redwood/fincorp/22201 (P2, pilot)
- https://support.redwood/eduos/7009 (P3, long lead)

Owen: Engineering note: streaming + toolcalls implies a framing layer for structured events. We currently stream raw tokens; runtime can't emit safe object boundaries without a protocol (delimiters/seq ids).

Tess: Runtime concerns:
- KV cache flushing if we invoke tools mid-stream
- partial JSON assembly needs sequence numbers and reassembly rules
- older SDKs expect final function payload at end; need compatibility shim

Maya: Draft launch criteria suggestion:
- API contract: event-frame JSON v1 (link to spec placeholder)
- SDKs: incremental parser support in JS + Python
- SLOs: first-event median <= 80ms, handshake p99 <= 500ms
- Error handling: automatic graceful fallback to non-streaming completion if parse fails

Liam: Sales context: AcmeHealth is gating production on this; deal ~ $180k ARR this quarter. Shipping a minimal supported mode (early text events + final framed function output) likely closes.

Maya: Two product options: minimal vs full.
1) Minimal: stream early text events, keep function call output framed at end. Lower infra changes, faster ship.
2) Full: structured event frames + mid-stream tool invocation support. Covers more cases but larger scope.

Owen: Rough eng estimates:
- Spike: 3d (design + perf assessment) INF-5234
- Minimal PoC: ~2w (runtime adapter + SDK parsing)
- Full mode: ~8-10w (framing protocol, tool runtime changes, rollout testing)

triage-bot: created INF-5234 (streaming-toolcall-spike) assigned to @Owen

Maya: @Liam can you confirm with Acme whether minimal contract suffices for the demo? Also need security signoff for event frames (no sensitive keys in frames).

Liam: I'll check in with Acme today. They indicated flexibility if they can start processing events early and get function outputs asap.

Tess: Ops requirement: add telemetry for streamed-frame success rate, frame parse errors, and fallback rate. We need these metrics before can enable broadly.

Maya: Next steps:
- @Sam: add sample payloads and repro to INF-5234
- @Owen: run the 3d spike and post perf notes in INF-5234
- @Tess: define telemetry + rollout gating
- Product to decide minimal vs full by EOD Friday

Owen: Starting the spike now; will post a short design note and perf numbers. If product picks minimal, I can cut a PoC branch.

Sam: Added sample payloads to INF-5234 and flagged Acme as critical.

Maya: Marking this thread as triage->backlog candidate. :white_check_mark:

Liam: :thumbsup: ping me for the Acme call if you want me there.

Sam: Will update the support tickets after product decision. Closing the loop here.
